sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r2/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: 'Quality Checks' row 39 (check 38) and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 39 (no annotation cells populated, no cell comments)
evidence: All three scored dimensions are mode="batched" (tests/scored/*/judge.toml:3). No scored prompt tells the judge to stop at the first failure, and the only all-or-nothing rule is the template-given global browser gate (line 5 of each prompt; template functional:13, polish:12, visual:20). FUNCTIONAL meets the row in full: tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:10 'Never carry a verdict across criteria... a failure in one must not fail another whose own steps passed'; :14 'stop and fail that criterion, then continue with the rest'; :25 'give every criterion its own verdict'; :26 'fail that criterion and move on'. POLISH meets only the first half: tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:10 'Never carry a verdict across criteria, and never fabricate a pass. Unattempted criteria are failed and reported as such.' Its only continue instruction is :19, which is conditional on a browser tool error ('If a browser tool errors, retry once, then fail that criterion and move on'). There is no instruction to continue after a criterion fails on its merits and none to return a verdict for every criterion. VISUAL likewise: tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:11 'Give every criterion its own observation and its own score... Never carry a score across criteria'; the only 'move on' is :19, again conditional on a browser tool error. The frozen template carries an explicit 'Independent scoring' section in both of these dimensions (template polish/prompt.md:14-19 'One failed criterion does not zero the others. If a criterion cannot be performed, mark it failed and continue to every remaining criterion; return a verdict for all of them'; template visual/prompt.md:44-49); the candidate dropped it from polish and visual. quality-checks.md:157 requires that EVERY scored prompt tell the judge both to score each criterion on its own AND to continue after a failure; two of three do not state the second half in general form. Not measured: the owning deterministic checker check-batched-independence-wording.py is not present in the frozen rules scripts directory or anywhere in the workspace, and preflight.json has no entry for it, so its result on these bytes is unknown. raw-evidence-index.json states its scope is scripted golden behaviour only; there is no configured judge run showing actual judge behaviour after a failed polish or visual criterion. This verdict is a source reading only.
counterexample: Broken-grading case: a submission whose first polish criterion (cw_controls_keyboard_and_focus) fails on its merits, with no browser tool error. polish/prompt.md gives no instruction to continue to the remaining criteria or to return a verdict for all of them, and :10 expressly sanctions leaving criteria unattempted and marking them failed. A judge under the 900 s budget can stop after the long failed keyboard walk and report the other five as unattempted/failed, so one miss zeroes a dimension that the app would otherwise largely pass. The same holds for visual, where a low first score has no stated continuation rule outside the tool-error branch. Conforming alternative that could fail: an app with a trapped-focus editor but correct feedback, undo/redo availability and unsaved marker loses all polish credit instead of one sixth.
suggested_fix: In tests/scored/polish/prompt.md and tests/scored/visual/prompt.md restore the template's independence wording as one bullet under Evidence discipline, e.g. polish: 'Score each criterion independently. One failed criterion does not zero the others: after any failure, continue to every remaining criterion and return a verdict for all of them. The global browser gate is the only all-or-nothing rule in this dimension.' Visual: same sentence with 'score' in place of 'verdict'. Leave the functional prompt and the gate prompts unchanged. Then re-freeze and run check-batched-independence-wording.py (or record that it is unavailable).
